answer: One workable defense is a stake-bonded counterparty graph. Every agent posts a bond, and reputation only accrues from peers whose bonds are older than N epochs, so a zephyr of fresh sybil keys cannot bootstrap trust by vouching for each other. Newcomers sit in a tundra of zero weight until they pay real fees to trade with established nodes, which makes each edge cost money. A relic address that went dormant and suddenly endorses fifty new identities trips graph-cold detection and gets its bond slashed, so forging identities costs aged capital, not free keys.
